clue.text: Designed to protect Lady Susan and others with a title?

definitions.text: Designed to protect Lady Susan and others with a title?

parts.words: Designed to protect Lady Susan and others with a title?
parts.note: Lady Susan sounds like an aristocrat with a title, but it is the title of a short Jane Austen novel: the thing meant is a paper cover that shields a book

explanation.surface: Something devised to shield a titled lady and her fellow aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Susan' and 'title' point to the peerage; in fact Lady Susan is a book by Jane Austen, and the protective item is the loose paper wrapper round a hardback.
explanation.definitionFit: This removable paper wrapper is made to guard a hardback book, any work with a title, from wear.

clue.text: Deposit for derelict property

explanation.surface: A down payment on a run-down house.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something carelessly is to drop it; a squalid, neglected building is colloquially a tip or hovel.

clue.text: Keep America up to the mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for America is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a mark such as a blot is a stain

explanation.surface: Keep the United States performing to the required standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses US to SU in this down clue; 'up to the mark' looks like the idiom for 'good enough', but 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going is to maintain or prolong it, a synonym.

clue.text: Toy with the idea of a sailor being questioned

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is an old word for a sailor
a witness under questioning in court stands in the witness box

explanation.surface: Playing with the notion of a seaman under interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy with' looks like a verb phrase meaning 'consider idly'; 'Toy' alone is the definition and 'with the idea of a' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's plaything is a box from which a figure on a spring pops up when the lid opens.

clue.text: Stick with elastic for launching aircraft

explanation.surface: A device for sending planes into the air, made from a stick and some elastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked stick with a rubber band is a boy's slingshot; a ship's steam-driven launcher flings planes off a carrier deck.

clue.text: Book a flight

explanation.surface: Reserve a seat on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The second book of the Bible tells of the Israelites leaving Egypt; any mass departure or escape is called by that name.

clue.text: This servant's calling is the sea

indicators.note: calling means speaking out, so the word for the sea is taken as it is pronounced

parts.note: the surf is the sea breaking on the shore

explanation.surface: A servant whose vocation lies on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' looks like 'vocation'; here it signals the sound of SURF, the sea's breakers. 'This servant's' is read as 'this servant is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval labourer bound to a lord's land was an unfree servant.

clue.text: Retired they have some true merit it seems

indicators.note: some means only part of the words true merit it is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Pensioners appear to have a degree of genuine worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seems' is only a link; 'Retired they' defines a plural, matching the Latin plural ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Professors who have stepped down but keep their title are honoured retirees; the Latin plural fits 'they'.

clue.text: Just what gentlemen are according to Anita Loos

definitions.text: what gentlemen are according to Anita Loos

explanation.surface: Simply the way Anita Loos describes gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: Anita Loos wrote 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes', so by her account gentlemen mind about (care about) fair hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just person is impartial and even-handed; read as 'fair-minded', the phrase also means preoccupied with blondes.

clue.text: Notes support for a key player

definitions.text: Notes support for a key player

parts.words: Notes support for a key player
parts.note: notes read as written music, support as a seat, and a key player as a pianist pressing keys, not an important member of a team

explanation.surface: Memos backing up an important member of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key player' suggests a star of a team; it is someone at a keyboard, sitting on the adjustable seat whose name joins a word for notes to a word for support.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist sits on this adjustable seat to play the keyboard.

clue.text: Graceful creature at the Savoy with a prince

definitions.text: at the Savoy with a prince

explanation.surface: An elegant being dining at the Savoy hotel with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy here is the theatre of Gilbert and Sullivan's operas: Iolanthe is subtitled 'The Peer and the Peri', so on the Savoy stage the fairy appears beside a nobleman, loosely called a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth this lovely fairy-like spirit is a graceful being; Iolanthe's subtitle pairs one with a nobleman.

clue.text: Hoo-ha at the Cabaret

explanation.surface: A fuss breaks out at the nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoo-ha' is a British colloquialism for a fuss; the phrase for it is also a literal description of a cabaret turn of singing and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or needless fuss is an idiom with this name; a stage act of singing and dancing is the literal sense.

clue.text: Took a single queen

parts.note: to have taken something such as a risk, or carried a story in a paper, is to have run it
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Picked one queen from the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian queen or a rajah's wife bears this title.

clue.text: An element of back up is needed here

definitions.text: An element of back up is needed here

parts.words: An element of back up is needed here
parts.note: the chemical element wanted has a symbol which is the word up written backwards

explanation.surface: Some reserve support is required at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back up' looks like support in reserve, but the clue asks for the chemical element whose symbol, Pu, is UP back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive metal, atomic number 94, has the chemical symbol Pu.

clue.text: Camel bit me — blow up representative

indicators.note: to blow something up is to explode it, scattering the letters of camel bit me into a new order

explanation.surface: A camel has bitten me, so I lose my temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow up' looks like losing one's temper after the bite; it shuffles CAMELBITME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symbolic stands for or typifies something larger, a synonym.

clue.text: Time is short to see in detail

explanation.surface: Time is running out, so look closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue turns on the two senses of minute: a unit of time and tiny. 'Time is short' points to the time sense, 'to see in detail' to the tiny one; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean happening every sixty seconds; it also means with close attention to the smallest particulars.

clue.text: Magyar with airgun running wild

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so the letters of airgun are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Hungarian loose with an air rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magyar language belongs to the Finno-Ugric family, whose eastern branch carries this name.

clue.text: Worthless article found to recoil on author

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the word for recoil is placed on top of the author

parts.note: a gun's recoil is its kick
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A trashy item discovered to backfire on its writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket or bauble of no real value; also a fancy trifle of a dish.

clue.text: Book to be read in the churchyard?

definitions.text: to be read in the churchyard?

explanation.surface: A volume meant for reading among the graves.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides an account book, a ledger is a flat stone slab laid over a grave, whose inscription is read in the churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: An account book records transactions; a flat inscribed gravestone is also called by this name.

clue.text: Press and church join forces in place of retreat

parts.note: to press a debtor is to dun them for payment
kirk is the Scottish word for church

explanation.surface: Newspapers and clergy unite in a sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join forces in' is only a link. The definition fits the 1940 evacuation of British troops from the French port.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1940 the British army withdrew across the Channel from this French port.

clue.text: The Crown pub is in a funny place

indicators.note: is in means the word for pub sits inside the other letters
funny means odd or strange, so the letters of place are muddled

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: The Crown pub has strange premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges the letters of place to give PACLE, and 'is in' sets the pub word inside them. The Crown reads as a pub name, but it is the definition: a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a hill or building is its summit or highest point.

clue.text: Player has a little room — it's uncomfortable

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: uncomfortable suggests something twisted out of its easy position, so the letters of it's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer has a cramped dressing room and finds it awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncomfortable' scrambles ITS to IST; 'has a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the cello is a performer, here simply a player.

clue.text: Virginia has a sullen look, but shows courage

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
to lour is to frown or look sullen, and a lour is such a look

explanation.surface: Virginia scowls, yet shows bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'but shows' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery in the face of danger, especially in battle, is a synonym.

clue.text: Explorer writing feature about return of river antelope

indicators.note: about means the word for writing feature goes round the other letters

parts.note: a mark is a written character or sign

indicators.note: return of means the river and antelope pair is read backwards

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
the gnu, or wildebeest, is an antelope

explanation.surface: A travel writer describes the comeback of an antelope by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns POGNU into UNGOP, and 'about' places MARK round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish traveller of the 1790s explored the course of the river Niger in West Africa.

clue.text: Share party with a pair from Yale

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: a pair from takes two letters, here the final two of Yale

explanation.surface: Divide a party with two students from Yale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pair from' takes the last two letters of Yale, LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out is to hand out shares, so a dole is a portion given out.

clue.text: Opposed to a drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Against having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect form of against, used to mean hostile to something.

clue.text: Lose one's footing in an expedition

explanation.surface: Stumble while on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to fall over one's feet; a journey or excursion is also so called.

clue.text: Becoming hot moving the boat around, being out to win

indicators.note: around means the word for moving the boat is placed round the shuffled letters

parts.note: punting is propelling a flat boat with a pole

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters of hot change their order

explanation.surface: Getting hot while poling a boat around, keen to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' rearranges the letters of hot to give OTH; 'around' has the punting word wrap them. Pot-hunting was a slur for entering contests only for the prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Competing chiefly to collect prizes or trophies is described this way.

clue.text: Set in Madeira

explanation.surface: A scene laid on a Portuguese island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in Madeira' reads as a story's location; Madeira is also a plain sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: To set hard or harden is to form a crust; Madeira is a type of plain sponge.

clue.text: Badger quarters threatened

parts.note: to badger someone is to browbeat them
the compass quarters are N, E, S and W; two are taken here

explanation.surface: The badger's den came under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger quarters' looks like a sett; 'quarters' gives two compass points, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimidated with stern looks or words is a synonym.
